Each case names its Runtime owner, actor/role, permission and data scope, required outcome, error contract, restart sensitivity, and required evidence kinds. Every scoped read and write requires positive and differentiated-scope proof (database-agnostic, by ordinary query/HTTP probes — never engine-level RLS posture; see G14); every protected operation also requires permission-denied proof. Writes additionally require missing-idempotency-key rejection, idempotent replay, idempotency conflict, persistence read-back and audit correlation. Project Actions additionally require one HTTP mutation per business intent, one Runtime unit of work, atomic commit, injected rollback, and concurrency conflict; atomicity is proven by `http_exchange` + `transaction_trace` + `persistence_snapshot` + `audit_correlation`. The denominator never reads frontend source or requires frontend evidence. Each declared Handler Connector call gets its own case bound to the exact connector, connection, provider, operation, execution mode and side-effect class; durable writes require worker restart and terminal reconciliation. Declared notification events require after-commit once-only durable refetch, and every external channel gets its own provider-terminal case. Every Report and typed list/search/query operation requires bounded page and stable traversal cases with a query profile captured on the same database cohort named by the managed process receipt: SQLite uses `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, MySQL uses `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, and PostgreSQL uses `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, all with statement/row-count observation and machine-checked index/full-scan classification. Evidence whose dialect or plan format differs from `runtime_identity.database_driver` is rejected; no second database or SQLite fallback is allowed. Its signed cursor must either encode the complete deterministic keyset tuple or bind an authorized source version to a bounded offset; a source-version-fenced continuation must reject source drift as a stale-cursor conflict. Automation Rules derive before-transaction rollback or after-commit restart/terminal cases from their trigger. Agent resources additionally require task cancel/retry/reconcile with terminal worker/audit evidence and interactive SSE disconnect/resume. A manual approval Workflow is proven as a durable process: start before the managed Runtime replacement, refetch after restart, decide real assigned tasks through participant APIs, and observe terminal persistence/audit; it does not claim `worker_terminal` unless the graph actually schedules worker-owned work. Scheduled jobs and governed report exports retain worker restart/resume evidence. Typed operations declared by acceptance `config.runtime_operations` must resolve to the pinned Runtime API and include both positive and denied rows for writes. Read and apply all 32 families in [production-technical-gates.md](production-technical-gates.md); a project may mark a family not applicable only from model-derived evidence.

Semantic oracles are strict. Each scenario uses fresh setup identities/records or names an explicit dependency whose passing evidence is current. A positive case must identify and observe its intended target with the required non-empty facts; a `2xx` paired with an empty collection, null result, zero aggregate, or different record is not proof unless that exact value is the confirmed outcome. A negative case must reach the intended stable status/error/concealment and prove unchanged durable state; an arbitrary `4xx`, `not found`, empty result caused by bad setup, or exception from a missing dependency is not the expected rejection. Scope isolation probes use otherwise equivalent requests against the same target through formal matching and non-matching Runtime sessions, plus the broader in-scope role when applicable. Runtime-owned identity/context values in setup and requests must come from the formal typed client, seed/admin path, or persisted Runtime result and be carried unchanged; synthetic claims or hand-normalized canonical values invalidate the case.

### Runner-first acceptance execution

With the denominator prepared and the managed Runtime healthy, execute the mechanical case families through the platform runner FIRST — before writing any harness code:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance run --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --cases standard --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The runner (capability `project.acceptance.run`, diagnostic report contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-run-v2`) mechanically executes the standard Action, Automation, Report GET-summary, Runtime read-route, Workflow, governed export and Scheduler families against the live Runtime and the exact sqlite/mysql/postgres database cohort bound by its managed process receipt, validates every artifact with the same `acceptance check` validators before writing it, and atomically writes/merges one complete `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2` document. External cohorts require the same explicit `DATABASE_DRIVER`/`DATABASE_DSN` environment binding already used by the managed Runtime; the runner compares only non-secret DSN/cohort identities and never serializes the DSN. It contains exactly one row per denominator case: `passed`, `declared_gap`, or `not_passed` with typed responsibility. Existing passed/gap rows are immutable; existing `not_passed` rows are retried. The separate `.domainry/development/acceptance-evidence/backend-acceptance-run.json` is execution diagnostics, not a second source of case truth. For every case the runner uses the semantic contract's exact actor and calls the authenticated Runtime `GET /identity/principal-context` resolver; Runtime returns canonical workspace/workforce/organization/business-profile/surface selectors, and the runner carries only those selectors into requests. Neither runner nor business harness may infer a user from role ordering, construct profile headers, or query Runtime-owned identity tables. Never re-implement or overwrite a runner-passed case. A `not_passed` outcome with `disposition:"runtime_failed"` is an observed contract violation — a product defect to repair at its owner, never a harness problem. Only `needs_business_harness` rows belong in the self-built harness. `blocked_dependency`, `blocked_platform`, `unsupported_runner`, `setup_failed`, `evidence_rejected`, and `runtime_failed` return to their named owner first; downstream cases sharing a failed setup are `blocked_dependency`, not independent failures.

Self-built harness code must be a thin assertion layer on top of [acceptance-harness-core.py](../assets/acceptance-harness-core.py): copy that file unchanged into `.domainry/development/`, then write only per-case assertion functions against it — never re-implement session/auth bootstrap, HTTP or database capture, artifact/evidence/results writers, resume state, retry/backoff plumbing, or any DSN parser/adapter. SQLite is stdlib-backed. For MySQL, install `PyMySQL` in the harness environment and call `AcceptanceDatabase.from_runtime_state(PROJECT_ROOT, state)` (or construct `Harness` normally) with no callback: core lazy-loads PyMySQL and exclusively accepts the managed Runtime Go-style contract `user:<password>@tcp(host:port)/database?charset=utf8mb4&parseTime=True&loc=Local`. URL DSNs, omitted or invalid targets/ports, and added, reordered, unknown, or dangerous query semantics fail closed; the password may be empty and is never emitted. Agent-written MySQL connectors and DSN parsers are prohibited. PostgreSQL retains the explicit advanced DB-API 2 `database_connector(driver, dsn, schema)` boundary. For both external drivers, core reads the random in-database marker and derives `sha256("domainry-managed-runtime-database-cohort-v1\n" + driver + "\n" + receipt.database_dsn_identity_sha256 + "\n" + marker_identity)` before comparing it with the managed Runtime receipt's `database_identity_sha256`; the marker is never itself the receipt identity, and copied marker rows at a different DSN identity fail closed. Missing or invalid receipt/marker contracts and identities are rejected without fallback. Core suppresses connector stdout/stderr, owns dialect SQL/EXPLAIN and DSN/password redaction, and never falls back to SQLite. Use `harness.session_for_case(case)` exclusively for the frozen actor/principal mapping. Register cases in `ScenarioGraph`; each setup receives a fresh opaque namespace, `setup_failed` is distinct from a product failure, and downstream cases become `blocked_dependency` rather than executing against missing residue. Apply `ReasonOracle` for exact positive, rejection, state, scope, and audit assertions before sealing evidence.

Execute only the remaining `needs_business_harness` cases through that real acceptance harness and project-provisioned non-human Runtime identities. The harness—not prose editing—writes typed HTTP exchanges, SSE transcripts, durable refetches, idempotency receipts, database snapshots, transaction and pagination traces, query profiles, audit correlation, differentiated-scope data, provider receipts, worker terminal observations, and restart observations under project-owned `backend/tests/evidence/**`. Self-built harness code and every intermediate working file live under `.domainry/development/**` from the very first file, never anywhere under `backend/**`: harness files inside `backend/**` dirty the finalized `source_sha256` and make every gate receipt stale, and the measured cost of that mistake is a full finalize/verify/package redo plus re-recording all evidence. Every structured observation references one real regular non-symlink artifact and its SHA-256; persistence evidence also supplies before/after hashes and, for replay, the replay hash. Results and every evidence document bind the denominator and Runtime identity hashes. Then run:

The result document contract is `domainry-backend-acceptance-results-v2`: copy `denominator_sha256`, `runtime_identity`, and `runtime_identity_sha256` exactly from the denominator and provide exactly one `results[]` row for every denominator case. A `passed` row contains `case_id`, `state`, and `evidence[]` (`path`, `sha256`); a `not_passed` row contains no evidence and requires `outcome.disposition`, stable `code`, `owner`, `root_case_id`, `retryable`, and factual `reason`; a `declared_gap` row uses the existing typed gap contract. `acceptance check` fails closed while any `not_passed` row remains. The business harness may replace only a row whose disposition is `needs_business_harness`; it cannot replace platform, dependency, setup, evidence, unsupported-runner, or Runtime failures. Each referenced evidence document is `domainry-backend-acceptance-evidence-v1` with `state:"passed"`, the exact case/denominator/Runtime hashes, and `observations[]`. An observation has `kind`, project-relative `artifact`, `artifact_sha256`, and only for `persistence_snapshot` the required `before_sha256`/`after_sha256` plus replay SHA when applicable. Each artifact is strict JSON `domainry-backend-acceptance-artifact-v1` and binds its kind, case, operation, Runtime identity, producer source receipt, capture owner, and typed facts. Accepted kinds are `http_exchange`, `persistence_snapshot`, `idempotency_receipt`, `sse_transcript`, `durable_refetch`, `runtime_restart`, `worker_terminal`, `differentiated_scope_data`, `transaction_trace`, `pagination_trace`, `query_profile`, `audit_correlation`, `security_posture`, and `provider_receipt`. Pagination facts bind stable sort/tie-breaker and cursor strategy; offset fencing additionally requires the bound source version and observed stale-cursor rejection. Provider receipts bind the denominator's exact connector, connection, provider, operation; a durable provider or notification audit also requires its outbox reference. A correctly hashed arbitrary text file or a typed artifact whose endpoint, actor, outcome, transaction counts, page facts, process/database identity, differentiated data scope, or provider terminal state contradicts the denominator is rejected. The harness must preserve secrets safely, but redaction cannot remove facts needed to prove the case.

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance check --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The check reruns model derivation, resolves the live managed Runtime cohort, verifies every raw artifact, and requires exact set equality with the denominator. Missing, orphan, duplicate, failed, stale, unbound, unknown-kind, artifactless, or `self_reported` coverage fails. A percentage, prose claim, Mock transcript, or evidence from another Runtime can never satisfy it.

### Incremental re-recording after a model evolution

The denominator's `artifact_manifest` digests each operation's dependency closure, so an evolution no longer forces a blind full re-record: evidence recorded against an archived earlier generation stays binding when a complete hash proof chain shows nothing its case depends on changed. After any evolution, with the new denominator prepared, first run:

```bash
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" project acceptance stale-report --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --results backend/tests/evidence/backend-acceptance-results.json
```

The report (contract `domainry-backend-acceptance-stale-report-v1`) classifies every case as `current` (evidence still binds), `stale` (with reason), `missing`, or `declared_gap`, plus counts. Re-record ONLY the `stale` + `missing` subset. For the runner's mechanical families, re-run `project acceptance run --cases standard` on the same results file: it applies the same per-case carry-forward proof, keeps every `current` result (report field `carried_forward`), rebinds the file to the new denominator, and re-executes only what it dropped. For the remaining stale business-assertion cases, re-record through the harness core's stale-list resume — `stale_case_ids(<stale-report>)` plus `Harness(..., stale_report=...)` and `pending_cases(...)` — which rewrites only the affected result entries (evidence file paths are reused) instead of rebuilding the results file. Then run `acceptance check` as usual: a receipt with non-zero `carried_forward_cases` is a normal, complete result — carried-forward coverage is hash-proven, never a gap and never `self_reported`.

Carry-forward pays only when the repair converges on attributable model items (actions, workflows, reports, export controls, scheduled jobs, agent tasks — plus a report's own `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`). Any other project source change — handler code, config, anything else under `backend/**` — and any shared-collection change (objects, roles, workspaces, automation rules, seeds, ...) shifts the shared digest and makes every case stale; prefer model-item-level fixes and keep every working file out of `backend/**` (harness location discipline above).

Finish the complete verification round before repair. Preserve every first failure and continue safe checks to collect the full finding inventory. `reconcile` never replays a product command and never overwrites a stale declared pass with a failed attempt: a strictly verifiable legacy cohort may receive an explicit migration receipt, a prior pass may be restored only from intact authoritative evidence, and every other case enters the typed manual repair queue. Recoverable `repair_required` exits 0 for shell continuation; only typed unrecoverable or corrupted/unsafe input exits nonzero. Then repair the named owner, create new round-specific Gates for invalidated commands, and continue; a terminal Gate and its first receipt are never overwritten or rerun.

The CLI makes this concrete for local structural checks. A failed metadata checklist writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/checklist-failed.json`; a failed source finalization writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/finalization-failed.json`; a failed `project verify` writes `.domainry/builder/receipts/verification-failed.json`. Each check is `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped_dependency`. Safe independent checks run in the same round even when a sibling fails; dependency-bound checks are skipped explicitly. Treat every `failed` row as one repair inventory and never treat `skipped_dependency` as a pass. These receipts remain L1 structural evidence only.

Run and bind evidence for:

- protected source boundary (`frontend/**` untouched under every recorded frontend mutation scope — no frontend typecheck/test/build set exists in this Skill because it never changes frontend source), and current source finalization;
- backend format, lint, vet, focused tests, full tests, verification, and package receipts;
- exact Runtime delivery/manifest identity and healthy managed Runtime;
- real non-human acceptance sessions and differentiated seed data;
- the complete operation x role x required-case inventory;
- the current acceptance denominator and its passing exact-set check receipt;
- allowed and denied authorization, application-layer data scope, sensitive fields, durable effects, conflicts, errors, and idempotency;
- Workflow, Scheduler, Automation, Connector, audit, outbox, and external-effect terminal outcomes;
- persistence read-back and critical-case restart persistence;
- cleanup of temporary records, processes, ports, and databases.

Acceptance in this Skill verifies backend logic end-to-end — real managed-Runtime HTTP/SSE/worker/database behavior. Browser-layer UI verification is outside its acceptance scope and is never a completion precondition.

The evidence Gate must bind evidence content plus applicable source, model/Blueprint, and Runtime identities. A later identity or artifact-content change makes the Gate stale. Re-run commands or regenerate artifacts; never reattach unchanged prose.

Evidence rules — tool-produced content only: every evidence file's content must be produced by a command, script, or platform tool and carry what makes it reproducible (the recorded command line, or its source plus sha256). The model never hand-transcribes, excerpts, or re-arranges content into an evidence file. In the TODO, an `Evidence:` line carries only the gate ID and path pointers; inlining more than one line of content there is prohibited.

## Failure classification

- Missing credentials, acceptance identities, differentiated data, explicit Runtime configuration, routes, permissions, sessions, Runtime health, or persistence is normally an implementation/Foundation defect. Return it to its owner and repair it in the same session; it becomes an external blocker only when every authorized provisioning/recovery path remains unavailable with recorded evidence.
- `verification_blocked` is allowed only when implementation is complete and every authorized execution mechanism for a required check remains unavailable after all recovery paths, or when continuing would risk data corruption/security, a result-changing business ambiguity has no safe authority, or governing contracts are objectively contradictory. Name the blocked checks, recovery attempts, project-local/external evidence, and highest reached level.
- Missing, partial, skipped, failed, stale, unbound, contradictory, or insufficient behavior evidence from an ordinary round is a repair finding, not a blocker, task exit, or intentional prototype. It can become terminal `acceptance_failed` only after every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair has been exhausted and the same frozen contract still fails.
- A non-blocking limitation may be reported only when it is outside the frozen scope and does not weaken an in-scope claim.

## Terminal states

This terminal verification sequence applies to `Execution scope: implementation`. A `requirements_only` batch may move directly from closed requirements/domain-truth Gates to `done`; that state proves only the accepted requirements artifact, reports no delivery or L1-L5 implementation claim, and must not imply Runtime or UI verification.

Record exactly one state:

- `done`: every in-scope Gate has current bound evidence at the required level, the acceptance matrix is complete, the finding inventory is empty, and no requirement is hidden, downgraded, or deferred.
- `acceptance_failed`: after the same-session repair loop exhausts every evidence-supported in-scope owner repair, implementation or evidence still fails the frozen acceptance contract. A first or ordinary failed acceptance round never qualifies.
- `verification_blocked`: implementation is complete but a required check cannot execute because no authorized execution capability exists.

Only `done` permits a whole-batch completion claim. Other states report per-capability results and the highest evidence level without upward summarization. Neither state is a shortcut around diagnosis: do not record it merely because validate/apply/verify/package/Runtime/canary/acceptance returned non-zero, and do not move a recoverable repair to user wait or another Host/Agent session.

Before completion, keep `Current stage: verify`, require the evidence Gate's `verify` status to pass, and run the TODO checker with `--expected-stage verify`. Change the stage to `done` only after terminal policy permits it; then require the Gate's `done` status and run the TODO checker again immediately before the final response.

The final summary states terminal state, implemented scope, frontend mutation scope, current delivery identity, tests/builds, Runtime result, highest evidence level, restart result, and open limitations. Never imply L4 browser evidence — it is outside this Skill's acceptance scope.

# Production technical gates

Read this file completely before model authoring, source implementation, Runtime integration, or terminal verification. These gates cover the backend and its published Runtime contract boundary. They do not assess page layout or visual quality.

## Gate semantics

A gate is `applicable`, `not_applicable`, or `failed`; it is never silently skipped. `not_applicable` requires a machine-derived reason tied to the current model and capability inventory. An applicable gate passes only with both its declared static proof and its real Runtime proof. Static validation can reject a structurally unsafe candidate, but cannot prove transaction rollback, cross-request idempotency, concurrent correctness, query boundedness, tenant isolation, worker recovery, SSE resume, or external-provider terminal effects.

The complete denominator contains the 32 gate families below. A project may have multiple cases for one family. The acceptance denominator must bind every case to the current model, Blueprint, CLI-compiled capability disclosure, generated source, packaged Runtime binary, and database cohort identity. Any bound identity change makes the evidence stale. (Isolation is proven behaviorally and database-agnostically per G14; no engine-specific security posture is bound or required.)

Evidence may redact secrets and personal data, but must retain the route or operation, actor/role, workspace, request/idempotency/correlation identity, status or stable error code, state transition, cursor or job identity, and durable before/after digests needed to prove the case. A prose claim, test name, arbitrary file, 2xx response, `queued`, `waiting`, or self-reported percentage is not evidence.

## A. Contract and delivery closure

### G01 Requirement-to-operation closure

- Applies when any executable requirement exists.
- Model/static: every requirement behavior resolves to its owning resource, typed operation, allowed and denied actor, data scope, fixture, expected terminal effect and acceptance case. Every executable resource has the inverse link back to a requirement and at least one operation/case.
- Runtime: exercise each changed operation and reference current prior evidence only for unchanged operations.
- Blocks: orphan requirements/resources, a single generic case used to cover several distinct operations, or model inventory omitted from the denominator.

### G02 Capability disclosure parity

- Applies to every Business/Portal endpoint selected by the project.
- Model/static: route policy, OpenAPI operation/schema, Runtime Domain API, Runtime Client method, owner, permission, scope, idempotency and stream semantics are an exact set. Static status is named `contract_ready`; it must not imply configured or scenario-verified behavior.
- Runtime: prove the selected operation is enabled and executable in the current delivery; provider-backed capabilities also require provider verification.
- Blocks: undocumented routes, catalog-only routes reported as scenario ready, generic request fallback presented as a typed client implementation, or stale capability hashes.

### G03 Skill, source, documentation and binary parity

- Applies to every release of this Skill.
- Model/static: Skill command examples, Go dispatcher, repository binary, packaged binary, supported command list, version, capability names and contract hashes match. Every fenced/inline `Correct`, `minimal`, and pattern example is machine parsed and validated.
- Runtime: packaged binary, not only the Go `run()` function, executes version/help and mandatory command smoke tests.
- Blocks: a documented command absent from the shipped binary, contradictory capability claims, stale examples, or installed-package evidence used for a different source tree.

### G04 One frontend intent to one Runtime command

- Applies to every user intent that changes business state.
- Model/static: the call-site inventory maps one intent to exactly one Runtime Action/command entrypoint. The Action payload carries all data needed to complete the intent; project BFFs, raw HTTP and client-side write orchestration are forbidden.
- Runtime: one interaction produces one governed request identity and one terminal receipt. Internal typed capability calls may be multiple, but remain inside the single Runtime-owned work unit.
- Blocks: open-table/open-shift/payment/submit flows implemented as sequential create/update calls, client rollback, a second repair call, or refetch presented as another business command.

## B. Command correctness and consistency

### G05 Single command boundary

- Applies to every multi-record, state-transition, settlement or external-effecting intent.
- Model/static: one project-owned Action or published Runtime System Operation owns validation, authorization, reads, writes and terminal output. It declares complete involved objects and effect sets.
- Runtime: request and audit traces show exactly one command invocation; retries reuse the same idempotency identity.
- Blocks: partial REST choreography, multiple endpoint calls required for success, or split authorization decisions.

### G06 Atomic transaction and rollback

- Applies when one command writes more than one record/table or couples a business write with audit/outbox/receipt state.
- Model/static: read/write sets close over Handler capabilities and the contract requires one Runtime-owned unit of work. Project source cannot open or commit its own database transaction.
- Runtime: inject failure after each write boundary and before commit; all business mutations, receipt, audit and outbox state roll back together. A retry produces one complete terminal result.
- Blocks: best-effort audit/outbox, artifact-first multi-step completion without repair, or tests that assert only the success response.

### G07 Idempotency and exact fingerprinting

- Applies to every externally reachable mutation and every retryable worker/provider effect.
- Model/static: a required stable idempotency identity is declared; fingerprints use normalized exact JSON values and include semantic preconditions while excluding secrets/volatile transport values.
- Runtime: missing key is rejected, same key/same semantic payload replays the original receipt across restart, same key/different payload conflicts, concurrent duplicates execute once, and commit-unknown is reconciled.
- Blocks: invocation-ID fallback for public HTTP, float64 conversion of money/large integers, pre-normalization claim collisions, or retry generating a new key.

### G08 Concurrency, compare-and-set and fencing

- Applies to mutations of existing records, capacity/inventory/balance changes, leases and asynchronous jobs.
- Model/static: each existing-record write declares either lock-before-write (`get_for_update`) or conditional/CAS update; leases carry owner, token and expiry fencing.
- Runtime: simultaneous competing commands prove the invariant, exactly one allowed transition where required, stable conflict errors, no lost update, and stale workers cannot commit.
- Blocks: read-then-unconditional-update, unstable retry loops, fixed leases without a completion/fencing policy, or merely serial unit tests.

## C. Domain and data integrity

### G09 Exact quantities, money and ratios

- Applies to currency, money, price, cost, fee, tax, balance, points, quantities whose scale matters, rates, ratios and percentages.
- Model/static: exact named types, currency/unit, scale and rounding owner are declared. Action input/output `currency`, `decimal`, and `percent` fields reuse a named Object source field and inherit its exact contract. Project Action/domain source cannot use binary floating point or ignore parse/range errors for these values.
- Runtime: boundary, rounding, negative/zero, maximum precision, replay and aggregation cases match the frozen rule snapshot.
- Blocks: `float64` money, silently defaulting parse failures to zero, string formatting as calculation, or current Settings used to recalculate historical results.

### G10 Historical truth, snapshots and corrections

- Applies to settlement, billing, commission, payroll, inventory valuation, points or other historical results.
- Model/static: policy identity/version, input snapshot, ordered calculation trace, result and immutable ledger entries are persisted; correction is reversal/adjustment, not mutation.
- Runtime: changing current Settings does not alter old results; refund/cancel/correction appends linked entries and preserves net invariants.
- Blocks: recomputation from current configuration, editable settled facts, or missing provenance.

### G11 Database constraints and physical schema

- Applies to every durable Object/table and relation.
- Model/static: not-null, unique, foreign-key/check constraints and indexes reflect the business invariant; index definitions include ordered columns, uniqueness, direction and predicate where relevant. Reconciliation compares physical definitions, not names only.
- Runtime: migrations succeed on the current managed Runtime/database cohort from clean and upgrade states (migration definitions stay dialect-portable across supported drivers); constraint violations return stable errors without partial writes.
- Blocks: application-only uniqueness, missing tenant prefix in uniqueness/indexes, or failed introspection treated as an empty healthy state.

### G12 Audit, outbox and receipt correlation

- Applies to every mutation, workflow/job transition, external effect and privileged read/export.
- Model/static: the contract declares audit event, receipt identity, correlation chain and after-commit/outbox owner. Terminal states distinguish intent, accepted, sent, delivered, reconciled and failed.
- Runtime: request ID to invocation/action/workflow/job/outbox/provider/notification IDs is traversable; failure/restart produces one consistent terminal chain.
- Blocks: best-effort audit loss, `queued` called delivered, replay returning an artifact whose audit/download chain is incomplete, or secrets in evidence.

## D. Security and tenancy

### G13 Credentials, sessions and tokens

- Applies to authenticated deployments.
- Model/static: no fixed/default production credential; bootstrap uses invitation or cryptographically random one-time credentials with forced change/expiry. Refresh consume-and-rotate is atomic and detects reuse.
- Runtime: fresh production-like database rejects documented/default passwords; concurrent refresh permits one successor; revoke/restart/workspace mismatch and token-family reuse behave correctly.
- Blocks: hard-coded `123456`, ignored configured password policy, non-atomic refresh rotation or fail-open lockout state.

### G14 Authorization, tenant scope and row-level isolation

- Applies to multi-tenant or scoped business data.
- **Isolation is enforced at the application layer and is database-agnostic.** Tenant isolation is the `workspace_id` boundary carried by every row and applied to every query; business row scope is the declared `data_permissions` scope/predicate evaluated against actor claims. This holds identically on every supported dialect. Do NOT depend on, require, prove, or claim any database-engine feature — in particular PostgreSQL row-level security (`relrowsecurity`, `BYPASSRLS`, forced-policy catalogs, per-connection `set_config`) — for isolation; the framework must stay portable across databases, so engine-level RLS posture is never a required capability, evidence kind, or `done` precondition.
- Model/static: least-privilege role and data scope are explicit; every scoped Object has a declared `data_permissions` entry and no scope relies on a database-engine policy.
- Runtime: at least two workspaces and differentiated actors with non-empty colliding data prove allowed access and cross-tenant/cross-scope denial through ordinary HTTP, Action, Report, export, worker and direct-query probes on the current managed Runtime database cohort.
- Blocks: empty-result tests passed off as isolation proof, role-header simulation, or any requirement for engine-specific RLS catalogs/posture as evidence.

### G15 Field security and assurance

- Applies to sensitive fields, high-risk Actions, exports or approval ceremonies.
- Model/static: read/mask/hide/write/export policy and Action output lineage are declared; enhanced assurance has a real issuer and binds workspace, user, Action, record, version and payload digest.
- Runtime: non-empty distinguishable sensitive values remain protected across Record, Action record/output, Report and export; missing/expired/replayed/mismatched assurance causes no mutation.
- Blocks: Action output bypassing field policy, empty sensitive fixtures, frontend-only approval, or `normal_login` used as enhanced assurance.

### G16 Hostile input, files, SQL, connectors and Agent tools

- Applies when the capability accepts files, URLs, Object SQL, connector input or anonymous/task capabilities.
- Model/static: parser-safe allowlists, size/type limits, clean-file receipts, SSRF/DNS/redirect rules and signed single-use Agent tool capabilities are explicit.
- Runtime: traversal/symlink/MIME deception, quarantine/scan failure, SQL CTE/subquery/UNION/comment/timeout, private/loopback/link-local/IPv6/DNS-rebinding URLs, and forged/cross-tenant/replayed Agent tool calls fail closed.
- Blocks: regex-only SQL rewriting, raw storage access, anonymous exception without negative proof, or emulator evidence presented as provider security.

## E. Query and resource performance

### G17 Execution-level bounded pagination

- Applies to every list/report/search with data-dependent cardinality.
- Model/static: API declares page size, opaque cursor, stable order and count semantics. Repository/executor accepts page/cursor and pushes `LIMIT page_size+1` or equivalent keyset/aggregate paging to the data owner. A result `limit` is only an output cap, not pagination proof.
- Runtime: first/middle/last pages at target volume show bounded rows read, query count, latency and peak memory; no full materialization precedes slicing.
- Blocks: fixed first 200/1000 rows, an Action `List` call without an explicit bounded page, full Summary followed by `paginate`, OFFSET traversal without a hard result bound plus a query-profile budget captured on the current managed Runtime database cohort, or async worker re-running the full Report for every page.

### G18 Stable traversal under change

- Applies to mutable paginated datasets.
- Model/static: every sort appends a unique deterministic tie-breaker and fixes null/collation behavior. The signed cursor either encodes the complete keyset tuple or binds an authorized source-version snapshot to a bounded offset; the latter must reject continuation after source drift.
- Runtime: equal sort keys plus concurrent insert/update/delete produce no duplicate or missing rows within the documented snapshot semantics; a source-version-fenced traversal returns a stable stale-cursor conflict rather than mixed-version rows, and retrying an unchanged cursor is deterministic.
- Blocks: custom row sort without an ID/unique tie-breaker, grouped sort without every grouping tie term, page-number-only traversal, unsigned response index, or offset continuation after source drift.

### G19 Index, query-plan and N+1 budget

- Applies to growth-sensitive reads, imports, exports, principal construction and relation resolution.
- Model/static: queries declare access pattern and expected composite/search index; loop-contained I/O requires a bounded exemption or batch interface.
- Runtime: the acceptance database uses its driver-equivalent structured plan (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for SQLite, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON` for MySQL, `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)` for PostgreSQL) and binds that plan format/dialect to the managed process receipt. Machine-checked access classification confirms index-driven execution on growth-sensitive paths; SQL statement/row-count observation at 1/10/100/1000 scale stays within rows-read and query-count budgets. Small-table full scans are accepted only when the bounded dataset fits one page and the plan records that scan explicitly.
- Blocks: index-name-only checks, B-tree claimed for `%substring%`, per-membership/profile/row queries, or latency logs without thresholds.

### G20 Timeouts, capacity, memory, streaming and fairness

- Applies to external I/O, database work, workers, imports/exports and multi-tenant shared resources.
- Model/static: request/job deadlines, byte/row/CPU/attempt/concurrency limits, cancellation, streaming/chunk ownership and per-tenant fairness semantics are declared.
- Runtime: slow SQL/provider/worker cancellation stops downstream work, returns the connection/lease, prevents late writes, bounds RSS and keeps a cold tenant progressing beside a hot tenant.
- Blocks: context timeout not propagated to DB, full artifact reassembly, process-local limits called tenant-global, missing job deadline, or unbounded goroutines.

## F. Asynchronous and external lifecycle

### G21 Workflow, scheduler and automation terminal semantics

- Applies when those resources are modeled or used by a journey.
- Model/static: triggers, branches, retries, dead letters, missed-window policy, run-as identity, before/after transaction boundary and terminal states are complete.
- Runtime: process/node/task/action effects and audit all terminate correctly across retry, cancellation, permission drift and restart; before failure rolls back and after-commit work is durable.
- Blocks: HTTP enqueue alone, waiting state called success, or schedule receipt not linked to Workflow/Action effect.

### G22 Connector and provider effect reconciliation

- Applies to any external provider call.
- Model/static: connection/provider identity, operation DTOs, timeout/retry safety, idempotency, outbox, response reference, callback/reconciliation and compensation are declared.
- Runtime: real configured provider evidence proves effect and reconciliation; retry/restart does not duplicate it, and uncertain outcomes remain explicitly reconcilable.
- Blocks: deterministic emulator as provider acceptance, SMTP accepted as delivered, or synchronous external call while holding database locks.

### G23 Worker lease, deadline and restart recovery

- Applies to asynchronous jobs, exports/imports, report workers, Agent tasks and background reconciliation.
- Model/static: durable queue, bounded claim, heartbeat, fencing token, deadline, attempts, terminal/dead-letter state and cleanup SLA exist.
- Runtime: kill the old PID during each critical window, prove a new PID with the same database/delivery recovers once, stale owner cannot commit, and no item is lost or duplicated.
- Blocks: in-memory queue, PID-less restart evidence, lease without fencing, or a worker test double.

### G24 Notification and after-commit delivery

- Applies when user/system notification is part of the accepted journey.
- Model/static: event identity, audience, template, durable inbox/outbox state, channel semantics and retry policy are bound to the owning terminal business event.
- Runtime: after commit/restart/replay, Inbox and channel effects appear once with correct actor/workspace visibility; rollback produces none.
- Blocks: direct pre-commit send, duplicate terminal notification, template-only evidence, or channel failure hidden by Inbox success.

## G. SSE and Agent lifecycle

### G25 SSE identity, resume and durable refetch

- Applies to every disclosed stream.
- Model/static: event type, stable event ID, cursor/`Last-Event-ID`, retention/resync contract, authorization and durable refetch endpoint are published. Invalidation is not durable data.
- Runtime: disconnect after a known event, reconnect with cursor, cover retained and expired cursors, restart and slow consumer; refetch returns the durable terminal truth without missing or duplicating effects.
- Blocks: accepted/result events without IDs, client with no reconnect path, connect-only tests, or process memory presented as durable replay.

### G26 Agent authorization and provider identity

- Applies when Agent/agent-task capability is claimed.
- Model/static: allowed tools/effect sets, service principal, workspace/role/scope recovery, provider configuration, model/policy and anonymous capability exceptions are explicit.
- Runtime: a real configured provider returns external run/model/usage identity; forged/escalated/cross-workspace tools are denied and source handlers remain inside frozen capabilities.
- Blocks: deterministic response fixture as Agent acceptance, bearer role simulation, or generic tool proxy.

### G27 Agent retry, cancellation, reconciliation and receipts

- Applies to asynchronous or tool-using Agent runs.
- Model/static: task/run/tool-call identities, lease/fencing, retry safety, cancel semantics, partial tool effects and reconciliation are declared.
- Runtime: cancel/retry/worker loss/provider timeout/restart produce one terminal task, durable tool receipts and reconciled business effects.
- Blocks: UI cancellation only, retry creating a new uncontrolled task, or final text without tool/effect receipts.

### G28 Multi-instance event/session durability

- Applies when more than one Runtime replica or failover is claimed.
- Model/static: session, rate limit, event backplane, cursor and worker coordination owners are shared or explicitly instance-local with limited claims.
- Runtime: requests/retries/streams cross replicas, one replica dies, and authorization, limits, fan-out, resume and work ownership remain correct.
- Blocks: process-local backplane/limiter advertised as global, sticky-session assumption without contract, or single-instance evidence used for HA.

## H. Operations and acceptance integrity

### G29 Observability, redaction and alert recovery

- Applies to production deployment.
- Model/static: low-cardinality metrics, structured logs, trace/correlation fields, redaction policy, queue/worker/provider/database indicators and actionable alerts are defined.
- Runtime: success and injected failure show the complete correlation chain; secrets are absent; lag/retry/dead-letter/capacity alerts fire and recover.
- Blocks: dashboard JSON or metric name existence alone, rows iteration omitted from SQL timing, or unbounded tenant/user labels.

### G30 Failure-window and commit-unknown injection

- Applies to every multi-step durable or external-effect lifecycle.
- Model/static: critical windows are enumerated: before write, between writes, before/after commit acknowledgement, before/after outbox/provider callback, receipt/audit finalization and restart.
- Runtime: deterministic failpoints cover each applicable window; retry/reconcile reaches one legal terminal state without partial invisible effects.
- Blocks: success-only tests, rollback tested only before the first write, or commit-unknown treated as a generic internal error.

### G31 Target dialect, migration, backup and upgrade recovery

- Applies to the current managed Runtime database cohort and the upgrade paths claimed by the release; code and migrations remain dialect-portable across the supported sqlite/mysql/postgres drivers (see G14), while runtime acceptance evidence is captured only on that cohort's driver.
- Model/static: compatibility matrix, migration order, lock/statement timeouts, rollback/forward-fix, backup/restore and retention/partition strategy are versioned.
- Runtime: clean install, previous-version upgrade, interrupted migration, backup restore and Runtime restart pass on the managed cohort with current roles.

- Runtime: checker independently verifies HTTP status/route/error, transaction/readback, cursor/query profile, old/new PID and DB identity, worker/provider terminal state, differentiated data-scope isolation and correlation facts.
- Blocks: arbitrary text satisfying an observation kind, self-authored `passed`, missing/orphan cases, evidence from another cohort, or an incomplete denominator exact-set pass.

`project verify` and package checks can establish only structural delivery evidence. Terminal `done` requires every applicable G01-G32 family to have current evidence at the level its claim needs. Only after every evidence-supported authorized owner repair is exhausted may the remaining gap produce terminal `acceptance_failed`. Do not remove the case, lower the claim, describe the capability as ready, wait for a routine user resume, or move ordinary repair to another session.

Commands:
  domainry-cli model preflight [--project <path>]
      Run authoritative local-only model checks and persist full diagnostics.
  domainry-cli model validate --json [--project <path>]
      Parse and validate backend/model/*.json, report the pending plan.
  domainry-cli model plan --json [--project <path>]
      Like validate, plus the item IDs behind each planned change.
  domainry-cli model apply --json [--project <path>] --go-module-path <path>
              [--environment <local|dev|stage|online> | --service <url>]
              [--allow-destructive] [--sync-only] [--channel <name>]
              [--cache <path>] [--cache-read-only] [--product-surfaces <csv>]
              [--target-goos <goos>] [--target-goarch <goarch>]
              [--evolution-audit-sha256 <sha256> --evolution-reason <reason>]
      Converge the Ledger to the model files, then validate, publish,
      resolve dependencies, materialize, and finalize in one pipeline. Existing
      Builder projects first emit a reviewable evolution audit; rerun with its
      exact SHA-256 and a non-empty review reason. --sync-only stops after the
      Ledger sync and checklist. Deletions require --allow-destructive.
  domainry-cli model export --json [--project <path>] [--force]
      Bootstrap backend/model/*.json from the current Ledger (one file per
      module) for projects created before the model-file workflow.

Agent metadata is resource-owned in the same model: emit `skills`, `agents`, `agent_tasks`, `agent_service_principals`, and `agent_entrypoints` from separate `resource` items in dependency order, each linked to the requirement it satisfies. Never place these collections inside the project item. Read [Agents and Agent Tasks](capabilities/agents-and-agent-tasks.md) before authoring them; exact fields and references come from the live Blueprint Definition consumed by `model validate|plan|apply`.

## Action declarations

An emitted `actions[]` entry requires `key`, `name`, `object_key`, `kind`, and `audit_event`. `kind` is the closed enum `bulk_operation`, `conditional_update`, `object_create`, `object_operation`, `record_delete`, `record_operation`, `record_restore`, `record_update`, or `transition_state`.

**Kind selection for Handler Actions**: a project-owned Handler must NOT use kind `object_create` — that kind carries the system `record.create` owner, and an Action with both a system operation and a business handler owner is rejected at **Runtime bootstrap** ("action has both system operation record.create and business handler owners"); no static stage (validate/finalize/check/verify/package) catches it. Use **`object_operation`** for an object-level Handler command (creation included) and **`record_operation`** for a record-targeted one; a Handler that creates records does the create through its data capabilities.

Authorization splits by ownership and both halves are enforced at compile time (`ledger.runtime_manifest_invalid`):

- A **project-owned Handler Action** (one that declares `handler`) uses the `authorization` block (`allowed_roles`, …).
- A **system Action** (`transition_state` and every other non-Handler kind) must instead declare `permission` — it compiles to Runtime `requires_permission`. `authorization` is rejected on a system Action, and a missing `permission` is rejected too. Runtime executes a system Action for any role holding that permission, so a role that must not execute a guarded transition (for example, "only managers close") must not hold the declared permission — or the transition must be owned by a manager-only Handler Action instead.
- **The `permission` key must be exactly two dot-segments: `<object_key>.<suffix>`** (e.g. `ticket.transition_close`, not `ticket.transition.close`). Runtime authorization re-derives the check as `<action.object_key>.<last-segment>`, so a three-segment key like `ticket.transition.start` passes `model validate` and one authorization layer but is re-read as the never-granted `ticket.start` by the second — every legitimate caller then fails with 403 `backend.permission.denied` at runtime. Platform permission keys granted verbatim in `roles[].permissions` (e.g. `identity.audit.view`) are exact-match strings and are not subject to this rule; it binds project-declared Action `permission` values and object CRUD keys.

Acceptance scenarios are strict Blueprint resources, not free-form test notes. Use only the declared top-level fields `key`, `name`, `description`, `actor`, `role`, `role_key`, `seed_data`, `seed_records`, `actions`, `attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_outcome`, `expected_error_code`, `expected_records`, `expected_reports`, `assertions`, and `config`; never invent shortcuts such as `objects` or `attempted_objects`. Express record/RLS expectations through `expected_records` or typed `assertions`.

`workflows` means a positive **manual** Workflow invocation and therefore requires `trigger_contract.type:"manual"`. Do not list `scheduled`, `action_completed`, or `record_event` Workflows there: the finalizer attributes them to their real trigger owner (the matching `scheduled_jobs`, Action, or Automation operation) and rejects a fabricated manual-run case with `acceptance.workflow_manual_trigger_required`.

The scenario-level `expected_outcome` closed enum is `""`, `positive`, `exception`, or `denied` — nothing else. Use `positive` for an expected success, `denied` for an expected Runtime authorization denial, and `exception` for every other expected non-success (state-machine rejection, RLS concealment, business precondition failure). Do not confuse it with the different `config.runtime_operations[].expected_outcome` enum documented below; the two enums are validated independently and values are not interchangeable. A `denied` scenario's role must actually be unable to execute every attempted Action: the composer rejects a denied scenario whose role holds the Action's authorization (`compose.acceptance_denied_role_can_execute_action`) — pick a genuinely unauthorized role or remove the grant.

### Acceptance composition rules enforced by `project acceptance prepare`

The denominator builder enforces these composition rules; authoring scenarios without them costs one repair round each:

- **Requirement coverage**: every `requirement` item — including purely declarative ones such as acceptance provisioning or navigation — must be reachable from at least one `acceptance` item's `requirement_keys` whose scenarios produce executable cases (`acceptance.requirement_coverage_missing: <key> resources=N operations=0 cases=0` otherwise). Cases come only from `actions`/`attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_reports`, and `config.runtime_operations`; a scenario carrying only `expected_records` produces no case.
- **Write denial coverage**: every write operation — each write Action and each write `runtime_operations` route — needs a denied-role case (`acceptance.permission_denial_missing`). For Actions, author a `denied` scenario with an unauthorized role. For typed routes, author a scenario whose `runtime_operations` entry sets **`"case": "permission_denied"`** (setting only `expected_outcome: denied` is not recognized); its default error code is `auth.permission_denied`, and its role must genuinely lack the route's required permissions.
- **Handler positive coverage is symmetric and DIRECT**: every Handler Action also needs a positive scenario whose `actions` list references it directly with an allowed role (`ledger.action_positive_scenario_missing`). Coverage through a Workflow branch that invokes the Handler does not count — a scheduler-driven or approval-driven Handler still needs one direct positive probe (e.g. the operator role invoking it with an explicit payload).
- **Every declared Object needs at least one seed** — including runtime-product objects such as reminder records or export audit/download artifacts (`ledger.seed_evidence_incomplete` names the missing objects); there is no exemption for objects normally populated only at runtime.
- Treat seed records as a closed typed graph before apply: every required field needs a value or declared default, every `$record:<seed-key>` relation must target a seed of the relation's declared object, option values must belong to the field value domain, and undeclared fields are errors. `model validate` reports these at the exact seed field; do not defer them to Runtime bootstrap.
- **Relation-typed `payload_fields` require `target_object_key`** referencing a **project** object; a Foundation target (e.g. an organization unit) is not resolvable there — pass the identifier as `text` and keep the Object field itself as the real relation.
- **Denied report cases are auto-derived — never author them.** A scenario referencing a report in `expected_reports` must use a role that IS allowed to read it (`acceptance.report_role_not_allowed` otherwise). - **CRUD/list/navigation coverage uses `config.runtime_operations` route keys** from the pinned Runtime Domain API `routes` map. The most-used keys: `object_query` (bounded list GET /objects/{objectKey}/records), `object_detail`, `object_create` (idempotency-key required), `object_update`, `object_delete`, `object_action`, `record_action`, `record_export`, `record_import_apply`, `effective_menu_list` (GET /identity/effective-menus), `business_notification_list`/`business_notification_stream` (SSE). Their nested shapes are closed too. `expected_records[]` accepts only `object_key`, `record_key`, `field_key`, `state`, `count`, and `values`; it has no `scope`. `expected_reports[]` accepts only `report_key`, `expected_run`, `expected_export`, `filters`, and array-valued `metrics` (use `[]`, not `{}`, when no metric is asserted). Assertions accept only their published typed assertion fields.

When a requirement consumes a typed Runtime capability that is not already represented by `actions`, `workflows`, or `expected_reports`, declare it under the scenario's `config.runtime_operations`. Each entry uses only `route_key` from the pinned Runtime Domain API plus optional `case`, `lifecycle`, `restart_sensitive`, `expected_outcome`, and `expected_error_code`; unknown fields, wrong field types, and route keys absent from the pinned Runtime Domain API fail during `model validate` (`evidence.typed_operation_route_unknown`). Use separate positive and `permission_denied` scenarios/roles for a write. The acceptance denominator resolves the route to the unified capability disclosure, preserves its real read/write effect class, required permissions, and SSE disposition, and rejects an allowed role labeled denied, a positive role missing the published permission, or a write without both positive and denied coverage. `expected_outcome`, when supplied, is one of `passed`, `denied`, `conflict`, `rejected`, `concealed`, `not_found`, or `failed`. Owners: `internal/builder/blueprintledger/ledger.go`, `internal/controlplane/authoring/validation/behavior_validation.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/action/validation/action_definition_validation.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/action/validation/action_permission_validation.go`, `internal/runtime/domain/action/service/action_assurance_domain_service.go`, `internal/runtime/bootstrap/composition/action_application_wiring.go`, `frontend/packages/runtime-client/src/index.ts`, `internal/runtime/domain/action/runtime/action_execution_runtime.go`, `internal/builder/sourcefinalizer/finalizer.go`.

`config.scope_owner:true` opts an object into Runtime department derivation even when no role currently uses `department` / `department_and_children`. The object contract is therefore validated from the field declaration itself, before publication and bootstrap:

- The scoped object declares exactly one owner anchor. A `user` field must use `config:{"scope_owner":true,"auto_assign_current_user":true}` so the authenticated principal, not a client payload, supplies the owner. Alternatively use a `relation` targeting `identity_user` with `config.scope_owner:true` when ownership is a canonical trusted relation. The validator rejects missing, ambiguous, wrong-type, and client-supplied user anchors.
- Declare **`owner_department_id`** and **`owner_department_path`** as optional text fields. Runtime also recognizes the exact camel-case spellings `ownerDepartmentId` / `ownerDepartmentPath`; no other aliases participate. The validator rejects a scope-owner object that lacks either derived field or declares either with a non-text type.
- Runtime derives both department values from the target scope owner's active primary Workforce assignment and overwrites client-supplied values. Reassignment therefore transfers scope to the target user's canonical department; it is not stamped from the invoking dispatcher and cannot be spoofed by payload.
- The principal's department facts come from **workforce data**: declare `identity_bootstrap.workforce_profiles[]` (`{id, identity_user_id, organization_id, work_status: "active", worker_no, worker_type}`) plus `identity_bootstrap.workforce_assignments[]` (`{id, workforce_profile_id, organization_unit_id: <department id>, assignment_type: "primary", status: "active"}`) binding every department-scoped actor. A `demo_users[].department_id` alone does NOT drive scope evaluation.
- **Bootstrap seeds are written without a principal, so their `owner_department_*` fields stay empty** — seeded records are invisible to department-scoped roles until a principal write stamps them. Plan acceptance so department-scoped positives operate on records created through real principals, and prove seed coverage through a broad-scope role.

## Handler cross-object writes are bound by the CALLER's data permissions

A Handler mutation on any object is authorized against the invoking principal's `data_permissions` — declaring the write in the Action's `handler.data_access`/EffectAuthority does NOT bypass row scope. If a role may invoke a Handler that creates or updates another object (e.g. conversion creating a `customer`), that role needs a truthful `write: true` data permission on that object (with a scope the candidate row satisfies — mind the department anchor fields above). To keep such an object "read-only" for direct use, simply do not declare its `<object>.create/update/delete` permission keys: the CRUD routes stay blocked by the missing permission while the Handler path works through the data permission.

requirements.md:3:本文档是 benchmark 的唯一需求输入。评分对照 golden-checklist(agent 不可见)。
requirements.md:13:- **technician(维修工程师)**:可见范围=本站点报修单;只能处理分派给自己的工单;完成维修时登记备件耗用。
requirements.md:14:- **ops_manager(运维经理)**:全站点可见;分派工单;审批保修减免;查看/导出报表。
requirements.md:22:4. 客户只能看到**自己的**报修单列表/详情(行级隔离);可见状态、分派工程师姓名、费用与减免结果。
requirements.md:25:5. 报修单字段:设备引用(必填)、故障描述(必填)、报价金额(精确金额两位小数)、状态、站点、分派工程师、创建/更新时间。
requirements.md:27:7. 经理将 `submitted` 工单**分派**给任一工程师并落站点;分派后工程师收到站内通知;撤派清空分派。
requirements.md:28:8. 开始维修(dispatched→in_repair)与完成维修由**被分派的工程师**执行;非分派人操作必须被拒。
requirements.md:37:13. 工程师完成维修时报出费用;客户在保修期内可由工程师发起**保修减免**:减免金额 < 500 直接生效;≥ 500 必须进入**审批流**由 ops_manager 审批。
requirements.md:38:14. 审批通过:减免生效、工单费用按减免后金额落账;审批拒绝:减免不生效并记录拒绝原因。两种结果都以站内通知发给发起工程师,且客户在门户可见最终费用与减免结果。
requirements.md:42:16. 工程师可见范围=**本站点**工单(同站点同事的可见,跨站点不可见);写操作(开始/完成/减免发起)仅限**分派给自己**的工单。
requirements.md:43:17. 经理全量可见。客户只见自己的(门户侧)。
requirements.md:47:19. 每天早上(工作日)由**定时任务**扫描:`dispatched` 超过 48 小时未开始维修的工单,给分派工程师发站内提醒(每单每天最多一次)。
requirements.md:50:20. 经理可见**吞吐报表**(按状态统计工单数)与**备件耗用报表**(按备件汇总耗用数量与金额,精确金额求和);工程师与客户无权查看。
requirements.md:55:23. Business Workspace 两内部角色登录后菜单差异化(工程师:我的工单;经理:全部工单、报表);客户门户有自己的入口与导航,不出现内部菜单。
requirements.md:56:24. 提供非人类验收身份:两个站点 × 各 1 名工程师 + 1 名经理 + 2 名门户客户(各绑 1 台设备);种子数据覆盖所有状态、两个站点、库存充足与不足的备件(≥3 种)、≥500 与 <500 的减免场景,保证每条需求可在真实 Runtime 验证。

Sensitive fields are fail-closed. Verify manager and self-service actors against live records containing non-zero values, because an omitted field cannot be distinguished from a legitimate zero-value in a weak fixture. Roles that must inspect Runtime audit evidence also need the platform permission `identity.audit.view`; do not assume a business title such as manager grants it.

**Platform permissions must be declared before they can be granted.** `roles[].permissions` may only reference keys present in the emitted `permissions` collection (`governance.role_permission_not_found` lists the declared set). To grant a platform permission such as `workflow.task.act` or a workflow-scoped `workflow.run.<workflow_key>`, first declare that key as a `permissions` collection entry, then add it to the role. A positive Workflow acceptance actor must hold one of exactly `workflow.run`, `ops.workflow.run`, or `workflow.run.<workflow_key>` (`ledger.workflow_scenario_run_permission_required`); prefer the workflow-scoped key for least privilege.

Surface audit and Workflow operations have narrower permissions than the underlying domain. `identity.audit.view` permits the identity-domain audit service, but Business Workspace `/business/audit-events` additionally requires `audit.business.read`; governance and operations audit routes use their own published keys. Team task views require their published Workflow team-task permission. Model the exact route being accepted instead of assuming a manager title or a broad Object grant covers it.

Business Workspace audit export is a dedicated Runtime report source, not an Object report and not the Tenant Admin audit export. Grant both `audit.business.read` and `audit.business.export`, then use `@domainry/runtime-client` `prepareBusinessAuditEventExport` with a stable idempotency key and `downloadBusinessAuditEventExport` with the returned short-lived token. The allowlisted filters are `event`, `object_key`, `record_id`, `actor_id`, `role_key`, `result`, `created_from`, and `created_to`. Without a complete object plus record target, Runtime forces the export to the current actor; with a complete target, Runtime validates the current record data scope at prepare and download. Empty results, unknown filters, expired tokens, permission changes, and scope changes fail closed. Never generate audit CSV or data URLs in project frontend source.

If a positive Workflow contains an `approval` node, the actor that resolves its task also requires `workflow.task.act`; execution and completion-proof semantics are owned by [workflow](workflow.md).

For `custom`, provide exactly one of `filter` or `predicate`. The compact `filter` grammar is only `<field> == $actor.<scalar_claim>` or `<field> in $actor.<collection_claim>`; use the structured Runtime predicate for boolean trees or relation paths. Non-custom scopes must omit both fields.

The structured `predicate` is a closed recursive contract. Every node requires `operator`, one of `and|or|not|eq|in`. Boolean nodes use `children`; leaf nodes use `field_key`, optional explicit relation `path`, `value_source` (`literal|actor_claim`), and either `claim_key` or `values`. A relation `path` is never an array of field-name strings. Every segment is an object with exactly `direction` (`forward|reverse`), `relation_field_key`, and `target_object_key`; the terminal `field_key` is declared on the final target object. Do not use invented keys such as `field`, `value`, `any`, `all`, `equals`, `value_claim`, or string-only path segments.

Runtime RLS paths may contain at most three relation segments, and every traversed `target_object_key` must be a declared project Object. Foundation entities are legal stored relation targets but are not traversable nodes in the project record-scope graph. To scope a member, coach, or other business profile to the login, declare a direct project-profile relation such as `gym_member.identity_user_id -> identity_user` and compare that field to the built-in `user_id` claim; do not traverse `identity_workforce_profile` inside `predicate.path`. The binding field's own contract (relation type, `identity_user` target, `unique: true`, ownership decision, role `required_binding_key`) lives in `identity-account-and-profile.md`.

Runtime always publishes only these built-in actor claims: scalar `user_id` and `business_profile_id`, plus collection `team_ids`, `store_ids`, `territory_ids`, and `warehouse_ids`. Other claims exist only when a declared Identity Profile Extension publishes them. Do not guess `member_id`, `coach_id`, `staff_id`, `workforce_profile_id`, `workforce_profile_ids`, or status claims. When a workforce-owned project record needs RLS and no extension claim is declared, project an `identity_user_id` relation through `identity_workforce_profile.identity_user_id` and compare it with `$actor.user_id`; extension claims are published by the Identity Profile Extension binding defined in `identity-account-and-profile.md`.

`owned_records` means Runtime record ownership; it does not infer ownership from a business relation such as `member_id`, `coach_id`, `sales_id`, or a seed key. Demo seeds normally belong to the bootstrap writer, so a member, coach, or sales demo user will see zero rows under `owned_records` unless ownership is explicitly authored by the supported contract. For PRD acceptance, prefer a truthful direct `identity_user_id == $actor.user_id` custom rule or a bounded relation path to that identity field, seed the matching identity relation, and prove the positive actor sees at least one intended row. A 200 response with `total:0` is not positive RLS evidence.

For a self-service profile Object, prefer the direct predicate `identity_user_id == $actor.user_id`. Do not compare the profile record `id` to `$actor.business_profile_id` unless managed Runtime evidence first proves a durable Identity Profile binding was created and survives restart. An Identity Profile Extension declaration or an `identity_user_id` seed alone is not that binding. Every positive RLS case must return at least one intended record; zero rows for member, coach, reception, or sales is a failed scenario, never harmless concealment.

Actor claim and terminal field types must also match Runtime's identity-policy contract. Built-in `user_id` is user-identity typed; `business_profile_id`, `team_ids`, `store_ids`, `territory_ids`, and `warehouse_ids` are relation-identity typed. Compare those claims only with `relation`, `user`, or compatible `text` terminal fields—never with a business `select` such as `status`. For example, `status == $actor.business_profile_id` is invalid even though its compact filter syntax parses; the metadata checklist inside `model apply` rejects it as `governance.data_permission_claim_type_mismatch`. Use a literal predicate for status values or compare an actual identity relation field to the appropriate actor claim.

## Reuse, extension, and prohibitions
Reuse Runtime authorization on records, Actions, reports and routes. Project code may add business preconditions but must not replace permission enforcement or trust frontend visibility.

## Examples
Correct owned-record role fragment:

```json
{"key":"member","name":"Member","record_scope":"owned_records","permissions":["class_booking.read"],"data_permissions":[{"object_key":"class_booking","scope":"owned_records","read":true,"write":false,"audit_denial":true}]}
```

Correct custom predicate leaf: `{"object_key":"class_booking","scope":"custom","read":true,"write":false,"audit_denial":true,"predicate":{"operator":"eq","field_key":"identity_user_id","value_source":"actor_claim","claim_key":"user_id"}}`. Correct boolean tree: `{"operator":"or","children":[{"operator":"eq","field_key":"owner_id","value_source":"actor_claim","claim_key":"user_id"},{"operator":"in","field_key":"store_id","value_source":"actor_claim","claim_key":"store_ids"}]}`.

Separately, the rerun exposed a real project-owned defect—the overdue notification omitted its required `work_order_id` template variable. I’ve repaired that Handler and added a focused regression assertion; I’m revalidating the invalidated source/package/Runtime chain before returning to the remaining fixture-owner rows.
